top_choice_rationale: P002 honours a specific, non-obvious prediction (the 2011 flat bands at a magic twist angle) followed by the 2018 discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states, reproduced widely and opening a new regime in which a strongly correlated many-body problem is tuned by one parameter. A citation limited to the prediction and the observation of the states makes no claim about the open pairing mechanism, which answers the maturity concern. The credit boundary (Cao, other experimental groups, earlier twisted-bilayer theory) is imperfect but acceptable. P001 is a close second: secure and cleanly credited, but a measurement capability that I weigh somewhat below a new regime of physics and with overlap questions against the 2005 and 2012 prizes. P003 follows with a real discovery but a more contested credit boundary and proximity to the 2016 topology prize; no award ranks last because several mature, valid achievements are available.
